0.2.0.lead: From this version on, this window says what changed after every update. This time: backups to download, a way to hold back upgrades and a much smaller database.

sections.title: Backups
sections.body: nexcrate now backs itself up weekly at night, daily or monthly if you like. Every copy can be downloaded as an encrypted archive and restored later, with the key for the stored credentials.

sections.title: Hold back upgrades
sections.body: Missing movies and episodes now load before upgrades, in SABnzbd and in qBittorrent. There is also a pause for everything already there when you switch it on, and a limit per day.

sections.title: Do not upgrade what is there
sections.body: When taking over from Radarr or Sonarr and when reading folders from disk, you can tick that the files brought along stay as they are. What is missing is still searched.

sections.title: Remove several titles
sections.body: In the library you can select several titles and remove them at once, with their files moved to the recycle bin if you like.

sections.title: Anime by scene numbers
sections.body: Releases that count episodes through are now matched and searched by TheXEM's scene numbers, as in Sonarr. You can switch this off per series and set the number by hand on every episode.

small: The database is much smaller: nexcrate keeps only what it reads from TMDB and gives empty space back at the start. The first start after the update takes a few minutes longer for it.
TheXEM is only asked about series it knows, and not at all for six hours after a failure.
A file taken over during an import now counts as filed in the log.

0.3.0.lead: This version guards against the wrong movie under the right number, says why nothing was loaded, and keeps the database free while large imports run.

sections.title: The wrong movie under the right number
sections.body: Some indexers list a release under another movie's TMDB or IMDb number. nexcrate now also reads the name: a release whose name fits none of the movie's titles is never taken automatically, never filed and never used as a replacement. It stays in the release list with a warning, and a finished download stops with the problem "The title does not fit the movie", where you can file it anyway. A whole title with more words after it, and a name only TMDB or Radarr know as a translation or alternative title, count only with the movie's year in the name.
sections.where: Title page › Search, and Downloads › Problems

sections.title: Why nothing was loaded
sections.body: After an automatic search each version says how many releases fit and, by reason, why the rest were refused. The same for series seasons and albums, in the log too.

sections.title: Replaced files in the recycle bin
sections.body: A file an upgrade replaces now stands in the recycle bin like a deleted one and comes back with one click. If its title has left the library since, restoring adds the title again, unwatched. When a file cannot go back to its place, the row says why: something lies there, the version has another file by now, or a Radarr, Sonarr or Lidarr connection feeds the version.
sections.where: Settings › Folders and naming › Recycle folder

sections.title: A broken archive counts as a failed download
sections.body: When a finished download misses archive volumes or wants a password, nexcrate treats it like a download its client gave up on: the release is blocked, its files are thrown away, and a replacement is searched. Removing a finished download that was never filed now deletes its job folder too, and only that folder.

small: Large imports, takeovers and new artists are written in parts, so other programs no longer wait minutes for the database. If it is busy all the same, they get 503 with a Retry-After.
A replacement after a failure goes first in the indexers' request budget, but never past a limit an indexer has made known.
A version shows the release its file came from.
Posters come from TMDB when the source cannot deliver one.
Saving the size table names the quality and the field that is wrong.
The automatic search no longer takes box sets for a studio album; deluxe and expanded editions still fit.
Titles in your language stay when a Radarr import runs.
A takeover no longer gives a file that already belongs to one version to a second one.
release.nex follows a file into the recycle bin and back.

0.3.1.lead: This version files downloads whose files arrive later, from a seedbox for example, and fits the library on a phone.

sections.title: Files that arrive later
sections.body: When a sync brings the files to the server only after the download finished, from a seedbox for example, the download used to stay behind as a problem because nexcrate could not find the files. nexcrate now looks again every few minutes for two days and files it once the folder is complete and no longer changes.

sections.title: Choose the folder yourself
sections.body: When nexcrate cannot find a download and has nothing to propose, you can now choose its folder yourself, for movies too. nexcrate derives the mapping for the download client from it and files the download right away. "Try again" is now also offered beside a proposal.

small: The library is no longer wider than the screen on a phone.
Searching while the automatic searches the same series now shows that search instead of an error.

0.3.2.lead: This version assigns more music files by itself and lets you choose tracks only the target release of an album has.

sections.title: Tracks only the target release has
sections.body: Once files of a download lie in the album folder, its release is fixed. A bonus track only the album's target release has could then not be assigned. "Assign by hand" now offers such tracks in a group of their own, and the file is named after the target release.

small: Scene style file names like "01-artist_name-title" are read without the artist, so the title fits.
Credits like "(Produced By …)" or "(ft. …)" in a title no longer get in the way of the assignment.

0.3.3.lead: This version waits for downloads whose folder a sync creates before the files are in it.

sections.title: Downloads from a seedbox, second part
sections.body: A sync tool like Resilio or Syncthing often creates the folder first and keeps unfinished files under a temporary name. nexcrate then met a folder without a video or music and stopped for good. It now keeps looking for two days, as it already did for a missing folder, and files the download once the files are there and the folder has stopped changing. The card offers "Try again" as well.

small: The card of a download without video or music now says that nexcrate keeps looking, instead of only telling you to remove it.

0.3.4.lead: This version lets the assistant create a profile again, and reads series folders that were added on the movie side.

sections.title: Profiles from the assistant
sections.body: On the last page, the assistant showed "This does not exist, or not any more" for a new profile under Profiles, and Save stayed locked. It built its overview for a version, and such a profile belongs to none yet. It now builds the overview for the kind of the profile, and you can save it.

sections.title: Series folders on the movie side
sections.body: A folder of series added under Movies was read as movies: every season folder became a movie of its own and stayed unknown. The folder now says when it holds season folders, and a folder you added can be read as a series folder with one click.

small: When TMDB stops answering during a scan, the job says so with the reason, instead of leaving the rest unknown without a word.

0.4.0.lead: This version takes the indexers from Prowlarr and keeps them up to date, gives every torrent a seeding goal, and clears finished torrents from the download client once the goal is reached.

sections.title: Indexers from Prowlarr
sections.body: Enter Prowlarr once with its address and API key. nexcrate takes every indexer from it, searches through Prowlarr and syncs on saving, on a click and every 15 minutes. What you change, add or delete in Prowlarr arrives by itself. There is nothing to set up in Prowlarr.

sections.title: Seeding goals per indexer
sections.body: Every torrent indexer can carry a ratio, a seed time and a seed time of its own for season packs. They come from Prowlarr, along with an import from Radarr, Sonarr or Lidarr, or from you. qBittorrent, Transmission and Deluge get the goal when the torrent is added.

sections.title: Removing finished torrents
sections.body: Once a torrent is imported and has reached its goal, nexcrate removes it together with its files in the download folder. The file in the library stays. The switch is on for new download clients and off for existing ones after the update.

small: When qBittorrent removes torrents by a rule of its own, the download client's card says so.
An indexer switched off in Prowlarr shows as switched off in a search instead of failing.
Minimum seeders now go up to 1000.

0.4.1.lead: This version says why a version without a default folder loads nothing. Until now it stayed silent.

sections.title: Versions without a folder
sections.body: A version without a default folder never searches or downloads by itself, and nexcrate did not say so: a series showed fitting releases and loaded none of them, and a title read "nothing wanted". The title page now names the missing folder, and for a series the season line says it beside the fitting releases.

small: The sentence about a missing folder no longer speaks of a movie when it is about a series.

0.5.0.lead: This version signs you in through authentik if you like, and guards the sign-in with a password with a second factor. No database change.

sections.title: Sign-in through authentik
sections.body: Enter the address of authentik and an API token, and nexcrate creates the provider and the application in authentik and lets in only the token's account. Then you link your account once. Only that identity opens nexcrate, every other one is turned away. Other providers such as Authelia, Keycloak or Pocket ID work by hand, and without a token there is a blueprint. Once linked, the sign-in with a password can be switched off; NEXCRATE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=1 opens it again in an emergency.

sections.title: Second factor
sections.body: After the password, nexcrate can ask for a code from an authenticator app. You get eight recovery codes that appear only once. Without the phone and the codes, python -m app.cli reset-second-factor switches the second factor off again.

small: Under a sub path (NEXCRATE_URL_BASE) a successful sign-in led back to the sign-in page. That is fixed.

0.6.0.lead: This version lets Bazarr read nexcrate as if it were Radarr and Sonarr, so Bazarr fetches subtitles for your movies and series. Still beta. No database change.

sections.title: Bazarr (beta)
sections.body: Switch it on, make a key with nothing but Read and enter nexcrate in Bazarr twice: under Radarr with the base URL /bazarr/radarr, under Sonarr with /bazarr/sonarr. Bazarr keeps a live connection and hears of a new or replaced file within seconds. Every version is an entry of its own in Bazarr, its name comes along as a tag, so each version can get a language profile of its own. A Bazarr update may break the connection until nexcrate catches up.

sections.title: Subtitles go with the video
sections.body: nexcrate records the subtitles Bazarr writes next to a video. They are renamed with the video and go into the recycle folder with it on an upgrade or a removal. Switching on looks once for subtitles that are already there.

small: With a second nexcrate at the same authentik, the authentik button makes names of its own instead of taking over the first one's sign-in.

0.7.0.lead: This version brings Discover: twenty movies, series or albums per list that your library does not have yet. For everyone without nexview in front. No database change.

sections.title: Discover
sections.body: Movies: New to get, Popular now, New and acclaimed, Classics. Only what is out on digital or disc shows up, movies only in cinemas are left out. Series: New series, Popular now, Finished and good, Classics. Filter by country, genre and original language. A click on a card adds the title, and you stay on the page.
sections.where: Discover in the bar at the top

sections.title: Discover music
sections.body: New releases, Played a lot now and Classics come from ListenBrainz, MusicBrainz's open listening record. It has a switch of its own, off from the factory: nexcrate only fetches the lists of the most played albums there and tells nothing about your library.
sections.where: Discover › Music, or Settings › Online services

sections.title: Not interested
sections.body: The small button on a card hides a title for good, and the list fills up to twenty again. At the bottom of the page you bring all hidden titles back.
sections.where: Discover, button at the top right of every card

small: On a phone the bar at the bottom now holds five entries, and "Settings" fits in whole.

0.7.1.lead: This version cleans up more thoroughly when you remove something: removing a title with its files also takes its finished torrent out of the download client. No database change.

sections.title: Remove a title with its files
sections.body: "Remove title" now has the box "Move the files into the recycle bin" that only removing several titles had so far. With it the files go into the recycle bin, a connected Plex, Jellyfin or Emby reads the folders again, and nexview learns that the title is gone.

sections.title: Finished torrents go along
sections.body: An imported torrent that was still seeding used to stay in the download client for good once its title went. Now it leaves qBittorrent, Transmission or Deluge together with its files in the download folder as soon as the title's files go, even before its seed goal. nexcrate never touches a file of the library doing so. The same holds when nexview deletes the files.
sections.where: Remove title with the box, remove a selection with the box, or deleting in nexview

small: If downloads are still running when you remove a title with its files, nexcrate now says so before any file moves.

0.7.2.lead: This version also removes the folders that are left empty once their files went into the recycle bin. No database change.

sections.title: No more empty folders
sections.body: When files go into the recycle bin, a folder left empty goes too: the movie folder, a season folder with its last episode, the series folder with its last season, and likewise album and artist folders. The release.nex nexcrate wrote there goes with it, unless it was changed by hand. A folder that still holds anything else stays, and a version's own folder never goes. Bring a file back from the recycle bin and its folder is made again.
sections.where: Wherever files go into the recycle bin, also when deleting in nexview

small: A connected media server then reads the nearest folder that is left.

0.7.3.lead: This version removes the whole folder when you remove a title with its files, as Radarr and Sonarr do. No database change.

sections.title: The whole folder goes along
sections.body: When you remove a title with its files, everything still in the movie or series folder goes into the recycle bin too: artwork, .nfo, extras. Then the folder goes. Deleting only the files leaves the rest of the folder alone. If the folder holds another title's file or a link, only the title's own files go.
sections.where: Remove title with the box, remove a selection with the box, or deleting in nexview

small: If a finished torrent stays in the download client because it is no longer in nexcrate's category, the log now says so.

0.8.0.lead: This version reads the episode names in the files: a pack that counts differently than TMDB still lands right. And nexcrate tries again what SABnzbd did not answer. No database change.

sections.title: Episode names have a say
sections.body: nexcrate compares the name behind the number, in the file or its folder, with the episode names on TMDB, in your language and in English. When a pack counts differently, for example because a double episode sits in one file and every number after it is one higher, nexcrate files by the names, as long as every file with a number carries a name and everything fits. When a file names another episode than its number and nothing else says which is right, nexcrate asks you. Common names such as “Pilot” or “Part 1” decide nothing.

sections.title: Assigning with a proposal
sections.body: Where a file carries an episode's name, that episode is chosen, marked “by episode name”. Without names, for a file with two numbers that is twice as long, nexcrate proposes reading every number after it one lower; the button “Use the proposal” fills that in. Below each file stands the chosen episode, in pink when it differs from the name or the number in the file.

sections.title: SABnzbd does not answer
sections.body: If nexcrate could not remove a failed job from SABnzbd, it tries again every round; after a day the history card says so. If handing over a replacement fails because SABnzbd does not answer, nexcrate hands it over again three minutes later instead of waiting for the next search.

small: When a series is called “Name: Subtitle” on TMDB, nexcrate also knows its files by the part before the colon, if it has at least two words. The search keeps the whole title.

0.8.1.lead: This version finds and files episodes right where TMDB lists a double episode as one and the releases count two. And signing in with Microsoft Entra ID. No database change.

sections.title: Double episodes TMDB lists as one
sections.body: TMDB lists some series with one long episode where TVDB and every release count two numbers. Every number after it is shifted, in The Office season 4 by up to four. Where nexcrate has no TVDB numbering, it now spots such episodes by their runtime on TMDB and counts them split as well. The episode name in the release decides which count is right. A release without a name stays ambiguous there and is not loaded by itself. Searching one episode also asks the shifted number.
sections.where: Search, automatic search and filing of series

sections.title: Sign in with Microsoft Entra ID
sections.body: The issuer may now be common or organizations as well, not only a fixed tenant ID. The form says what Entra needs: the redirect address with https and, if you like, the email address as an optional claim.
sections.where: Settings › System › Account › Another provider or by hand

small: When a file carries the name of an episode outside its download, “Assign by hand” chooses that episode all the same.
An episode name of four letters such as “Geld” now counts as a name, no longer as a common word.

0.9.0.lead: Signing in now works with several providers at once, one account per person. The first start adds two tables and copies the database first.

sections.title: Several sign-in providers, one account
sections.body: Add as many OpenID Connect providers as you like (authentik, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Authelia, Pocket ID). Each has its own button on the sign-in page and its own redirect address. A person links each provider once; an identity that is not linked is turned away, however the provider is set up. authentik is set up in one step from its address and a token. A provider you had before moves over at the first start and keeps its redirect address.

sections.title: Sign-in with a password can be switched off
sections.body: Once a provider is linked, the password can be switched off. If the last provider goes away, the password opens again by itself. To open it by hand, start nexcrate once with NEXCRATE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=1.

sections.title: Asking before the public address changes
sections.body: When authentik or a provider you entered by hand still knows the old redirect address, changing the public address asks first and says what to renew.

sections.title: Behind a reverse proxy that ends TLS
sections.body: nexcrate believes X-Forwarded-Proto only from the addresses in FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS (default 127.0.0.1). Name the address your proxy connects from, for example the gateway of the Docker network, or the redirect address is built with http.

small: Someone not signed in can no longer lock the owner out of the sign-in by sending wrong requests.
Mails carry a Date header. Some providers dropped them silently without one.
The first start of this version copies the database before it adds the new tables. On a large library that takes a while.

0.9.1.lead: A small release for nexcrate behind a reverse proxy: it reads the scheme the way the proxy wrote it, and trusts no proxy until you name it.

sections.title: Behind a reverse proxy
sections.body: nexcrate now takes the rightmost value of X-Forwarded-Proto, whatever its case, so a value like “http, https” from two proxies counts as https. FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS is empty by default (it was 127.0.0.1): name the address your proxy connects from, for example the gateway of the Docker network. With the variable already set, as most setups behind TLS have it, nothing changes. A proxy on the same machine with host networking needs FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS=127.0.0.1.

0.9.2.lead: A small release from issue #12: clearer words where nexcrate cannot find a download, and SABnzbd jobs that no longer stay behind.

sections.title: When nexcrate cannot find a download
sections.body: A download whose files nexcrate cannot find now says why no mapping was proposed. The card shows the path the download client reported. Found in more than one place, every place is listed and one click takes the right one. If the search stopped before it saw all folders, Choose the folder is there. If nexcrate looked everywhere and found nothing, the card says the download folder is probably not mounted in the container and lists the folders nexcrate sees.

sections.title: What the card of a download client counts
sections.body: The card called every unfinished download running, also finished ones waiting for the import and problems that sit in the client's history. It now names the three apart, and the problems lead to Downloads, Problems.

small: A movie that came with bonus clips no longer keeps its SABnzbd job and folder after the import: clips at most half the size of the movie go with the folder, as in Radarr.

0.9.3.lead: A small release from issue #13: when nexcrate refuses a default folder, you now see why.

sections.title: Choosing a default folder
sections.body: When nexcrate refused the chosen folder, for example because it may not write into it or because it already belongs to another version, the message stood below the folder list. With many subfolders it lay outside the window, and Take this folder seemed to do nothing. It now stands above the buttons.

small: The log now names every refusal of a chosen folder with its reason.

0.9.4.lead: Starting fresh and reading folders now leads straight into the library: nexcrate says what is still missing and lets you settle it right there.

sections.title: Reading folders without a dead end
sections.body: Reading worked without a version and without a TMDB token, but then everything stayed under Unknown and the library stayed empty. The page now says at the top what is still missing. You can create the version right there, and the folder you read can become its default folder. The Assign dialog offers the same.

sections.title: After reading
sections.body: The page says how many folders wait for assigning, jumps to the list on request and opens the first tab that holds something. Before, it stood on the empty Restore tab. An empty library names the folders that still wait, too.

sections.title: No more blank page
sections.body: When a page cannot be shown, it now says what happened, with Reload and the way back to the library. nexcrate writes the error into its log at the same time.

small: When no name names a source, the quality follows the file type, as in Radarr. The Assign dialog now says so instead of “from the name”.

1.0.0.lead: An app on the phone now connects with a QR code, and the interface for programs can search and discover as you do in the browser.

sections.title: Connect the iPhone app with a QR code
sections.body: API keys has a new button, Connect the iPhone app. It shows a QR code; the app scans it and gets a key of its own, without typing an address or a key. The code holds ten minutes and only once. A code nobody scanned leaves no key behind; a key the app took stands in the list afterwards and can be revoked there.

sections.title: Search by name
sections.body: Programs find movies and series at TMDB and artists and albums at MusicBrainz by their name, under /api/v1/search. Each hit says whether the library has it and can be requested right away. A key with read is enough.

sections.title: Discover for programs
sections.body: The lists of the Discover page are also under /api/v1/discover now, with the same filters and without what you have already. Not interested needs the scope request.

small: A single movie or series under /api/v1 now carries its overview, runtime and genres, and every download names its download client.
The folder list shows the same quality as the Assign dialog, so By file type where the name names no source.

1.1.0.lead: Programs get an overview of every movie and series with plot, rating and cast, also for titles that are not in the library yet.

sections.title: Plot and cast for programs
sections.body: /api/v1/about gives a movie's or series' plot, tagline, runtime, genres, TMDB's rating, who directed or created it, and up to twenty of the cast with role and picture. It works for titles of the library and for those you are about to add. nexcrate asks TMDB once per title and language and keeps the answer for seven days. A key with read is enough.

small: The interface's library stays as it is: the overview stands only with a single title, so its change numbers do not move.

1.2.0.lead: Lingarr translates subtitles and only knows Radarr and Sonarr. nexcrate now answers it as both, as it already does for Bazarr.

sections.title: Lingarr (beta)
sections.body: Lingarr now reads movies and series straight from nexcrate. In Lingarr, under Settings, Integrations, enter the two addresses nexcrate shows you instead of Radarr and Sonarr, with a key that has nothing but read. Every version is an entry of its own there. Tested with Lingarr 1.4.0.

sections.title: Subtitles come along
sections.body: Once a day nexcrate looks for subtitles next to the videos. What Lingarr or Bazarr wrote there then goes with its video: when it is renamed, upgraded or removed.

small: The tab Bazarr is now called Bazarr and Lingarr; the switch and the key work for both.
Series now name their seasons to programs that read nexcrate as Sonarr, and episodes can be asked for season by season.

1.2.1.lead: A small release from issue #15: Lingarr now takes nexcrate's key.

sections.title: Keys for Lingarr
sections.body: Lingarr's settings page only takes a Radarr or Sonarr key of exactly 32 characters, and nexcrate's keys had 47, so Lingarr refused them with API Key must be 32 characters. New keys now have 32 characters. To connect Lingarr, make a new key with nothing but read and enter it in both fields.

small: Keys you already have keep working everywhere; only keys made from now on are shorter.

1.2.2.lead: A small release from issue #18: the numbers on the title page now lead to TMDB, TVDB and IMDb.

sections.title: Numbers as links
sections.body: Below the overview of a movie or a series stand its numbers at TMDB, TVDB and IMDb. A click now opens the title's page there, in a new tab.

small: With the version check switched off, nexcrate no longer reports a newer release.

1.2.3.lead: A small release from issue #20: when another program moves a download to another category, nexcrate now says so instead of taking it for gone.

sections.title: Moved, not gone
sections.body: When a download is missing from nexcrate's category, nexcrate looks for it in the download client by its hash or its number. If it is still there, the card says in which category, whether it is paused and how far it is. Take back puts it into nexcrate's category again and goes on loading. Remove takes it out of the client as well, with its files, by default. nexcrate files nothing from the other category.

small: This works with qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission from 4.0, SABnzbd and NZBGet; with SABnzbd and NZBGet for jobs in the queue.
/api/v1 knows the problem moved_in_client and the action take_back.

1.3.0.lead: Kodi joins as a fourth media server, and the automatic album search no longer loads a release again and again whose files are worse than its name says (issue #22).

sections.title: Kodi as a media server
sections.body: Next to Plex, Jellyfin and Emby you can now add Kodi. nexcrate tells it about new files over Kodi's API, with or without the username and password of its web server. Video sources count for movies and series, music sources for music.

sections.title: No album on an endless loop
sections.body: When a release promises FLAC in its name and brings MP3, it goes on the album's blocklist after filing and is not loaded again by itself. Also, nexcrate loads an album by itself at most three times in 24 hours, whatever the reason. Search automatically now still works.

small: When mapping the paths of a media server, the dialog suggests the folders the server names for its libraries. Another folder can still be typed.

1.3.1.lead: A small release from issue #22: the automatic album search no longer takes the release the album's files came from.

sections.title: Not the same release again
sections.body: When an album's files came from one release, the search now refuses that release. Until now a single lower file the release does not replace could keep the album below its target, and the same release was loaded again and again. Other releases of the album still load. In the search by hand it shows as a reason on the release and can be confirmed.

small: This also covers releases filed before 1.3.0, which are on no blocklist for that reason.

1.3.2.lead: A small release from issue #23: nexcrate keeps working when the browser translates the page.

sections.title: Translated pages no longer fall over
sections.body: When Chrome or an extension translates the page, the browser swaps every piece of text for its own elements. As soon as a button then showed its loading spinner, for example when testing the TMDB connection, creating an API key or assigning a profile, nexcrate could no longer draw the page. Buttons now work on a translated page too, and the rest of the interface no longer falls over when text has been swapped out.

small: On a translated page, something that appears may sit at the end of its line instead of its usual place. The page keeps working.

1.4.0.lead: A release for music: filed files can be moved to another track by hand, and the track list says when a release named its files wrong.

sections.title: Move filed files
sections.body: In the “Assign by hand” dialog of an album download, the files already in the album folder now have a choice as well. Pick another track or “Fits no track, file anyway”, and nexcrate takes the file out of the album folder on filing and files it on the chosen track with a new name and new tags. Two files can also swap their tracks.

sections.title: Wrongly named releases
sections.body: Some releases name their files after the wrong song. When nexcrate filed such a file by its fingerprint, it looked like a wrong assignment. Now the file in the track list says which track its name in the download names and that the fingerprint found another one.

small: A file in the album folder cannot be set to “not filed” in the dialog. The album page has “This file into the recycle bin” for that.

1.4.1.lead: No new feature this time, but news: nexcrate is now available as an app for iPhone and iPad.

sections.title: nexcrate on the App Store
sections.body: The app shows your movies, series and music with every version. You add titles, follow downloads, sort out problems and see in the calendar what comes out soon. It is free and talks only to your own nexcrate. To connect it, scan the QR code under “Connect the iPhone app”.

sections.title: Android: testers wanted
sections.body: We would like to build an app for Android as well. Before Google lets a new app into the Play Store, it has to run in a closed test with 20 testers. If you have an Android device and would like to help, sign up in the discussion on GitHub.

1.5.0.lead: You can now import files you got yourself: from any folder nexcrate sees, for a movie, a series or an album.

sections.title: Import from a folder
sections.body: For files nexcrate could not or would not load. Choose a folder, see what lies in it, then pick the title and the version. nexcrate files it like a download, with its naming, and the old file goes into the recycle bin. What it cannot place, it asks you as usual. Your files stay where they are: nexcrate links or copies them and never moves or deletes them.

small: The folder has to be mounted into the container, as nexcrate only sees mounted folders. A folder inside the library folder of the version is refused.
Series and albums have to be in the library first. A movie from TMDB is added by the import.
